scenario.question: This is the deck's MODAL board: Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3) is our only creature, we have five untapped lands ({R}{R}{R}{R}{C}) and our hand is NOT known. seat-2 (jarad) 40 life, no creature. seat-3 (abaddon) 10 life, Abaddon the Despoiler (5/5) untapped. seat-4 (sythis) 20 life, Heliod Sun-Crowned (5/5) and Setessan Champion (1/3) untapped, plus Sphere of Safety AND the Aura Abundant Growth. (a) Using only the battlefield and its mana, what is the most damage we can deal to any one opponent this turn, and what prevents more? State Sphere of Safety's X explicitly and cite how it is computed. (b) What is the minimum a card in hand must do for Zada's triggered ability to copy it across our board FROM THIS BOARD STATE? Cite the rule for the 'targets only' condition.
notes: RE-LIFTED ON A FIXED BRIDGE (2026-09-28). The first lift (stack 009, now superseded) DROPPED EVERY AURA — they resolved as `Name (id) - Attach to X` and were discarded as instants. seat-4's Abundant Growth is now on the board, which is exactly the permanent that changes Sphere of Safety's X. The superseded resolution reasoned from X = 2.

WHY THIS BOARD. It is the deck's MODAL shape. Across 100 seeded games our seat had the commander out on 249 turns; even with tokens now reconstructed, a board of six or more other bodies occurs on about a fifth of them, and Zada alone or with one other is the common case.

HAND UNKNOWN BY CONSTRUCTION, and here that IS the finding: with five mana and the commander in play, what this deck can do depends on a card the log cannot show. Describe the REQUIRED PROPERTIES of a card, never a named one.

Each copy targets a different one of those creatures.' -- one triggered ability and no activated ability. card_membership: Zada is in the deck, NOT_IN_THE_DECK is empty.

The five lands produce at most {R}{R}{R}{R}{C} -- four red and one colourless, and the colourless can never pay a red pip. That is what the BATTLEFIELD produces, and it is not a ceiling on the turn: the hand is {unknown: 5} by construction and the 99 holds six mana-producing instants and sorceries (Rite of Flame, Pyretic Ritual, Seething Song, Battle Hymn, Brightstone Ritual, Mana Geyser), so a hand we may not assume could raise it. No permanent we control has a damage-dealing ability, so on the battlefield the five mana has no outlet at all and COMBAT DAMAGE is the only route to damage this turn. Zada's 3 power is therefore the ceiling on every damage figure below. (The only ability on any board that deals damage to a player is seat-3's own Talisman of Creativity -- 'This artifact deals 1 damage to you' -- and nothing we control can make seat-3 tap it.)

steps.action: Walk the combat phase and name every window in which an opponent may act, BEFORE pricing any single attack. With one creature we attack exactly one seat: the active player announces which player each chosen creature is attacking, and in a game that allows attacking multiple players a player may still choose to attack only one.
steps.effect: The windows, in order: declare attackers step -- the declaration is a turn-based action, and then the active player gets priority and all players pass in turn; declare blockers step -- blockers are declared, and then the active player gets priority again; then the combat damage step; then end of combat, where the active player gets priority once more. TWO of those windows sit before combat damage and both are open to the defender. This is what bounds every 'guaranteed' claim below. seat-2's lift records EIGHT cards in hand (estimate) and THREE untapped lands (Undergrowth Stadium, Swamp, Overgrown Tomb), so seat-2 can act with mana in both pre-damage windows -- removal, a fog, a prevention effect, or a flash body, and a creature can even be put onto the battlefield BLOCKING after attackers are declared. seat-4 is recorded at 0 cards in hand with all six lands tapped, and seat-3 at 0 cards in hand with all five lands tapped (its untapped Talisman of Creativity and Fellwar Stone could pay for something, but the recorded hand is empty), so for those two seats the pre-damage windows are empty on the board as lifted. The asymmetry in the pod is therefore real and it runs the opposite way from the superseded resolution's: the only seat with resources to answer an attack is seat-2, the one that cannot block.

steps.action: Line A -- declare Zada attacking seat-2 (jarad-graveyard, 40 life). seat-2's board as lifted is exactly three lands and no creature; Jarad, Golgari Lich Lord is in the command zone with 0 casts. No enchantment, so no attack tax.
steps.effect: The declaration is legal and free. seat-2 controls no creature, so it cannot DECLARE a blocker at all; Zada is unblocked and assigns combat damage equal to her power, 3, to seat-2: 40 -> 37. The exact claim is 3 DAMAGE THAT NO BLOCK CAN PREVENT -- not guaranteed damage. Calling it guaranteed would treat our five unknown cards as unusable while treating seat-2's eight cards and three untapped lands as nonexistent, and that asymmetry is not defensible: from step 3 seat-2 holds priority with open mana in both pre-damage windows, and the flash-blocker window established in step 3 (509.4) is live inside one of them. On value this is also the worst of the three seats: 3 into 40 is 7.5% of that life total, about fourteen more identical turns, against the highest life in the pod.

The same state-based-action check that destroys her also lets her owner put her into the command zone, and extras.reconstruction_notes records that this AI always takes that replacement -- so she is recastable at {3}{R} plus commander tax. Damage to seat-3 happens only if seat-3 declines to block, which is the defending player's choice and not a rules guarantee. Unblocked it is 10 -> 7, the most valuable 3 damage on the board; blocked it is 0 damage and a recast. Line B remains the wrong line, for this reason rather than the old one.

steps.action: Line C -- declare Zada attacking seat-4 (sythis-enchantress, 20 life), which requires paying Sphere of Safety's tax. Card text read from the corpus: 'Creatures can't attack you or planeswalkers you control unless their controller pays {X} for each of those creatures, where X is the number of enchantments you control.' X is defined by the ability rather than chosen, and it is computed by counting the permanents seat-4 controls that have the card type ENCHANTMENT. Enumerate all eleven of seat-4's recorded permanents by type line: Sphere of Safety 'Enchantment' -- COUNTS. Heliod, Sun-Crowned 'Legendary Enchantment Creature -- God' -- COUNTS. Abundant Growth 'Enchantment -- Aura' -- COUNTS, since Aura is a subtype of enchantment and an Aura is therefore an enchantment. Setessan Champion 'Creature -- Human Warrior' -- no. Sol Ring 'Artifact' -- no. Plains, Forest, Plains, Forest, Brushland, Overgrown Farmland -- six lands, no.
steps.effect: SPHERE OF SAFETY'S X = 3, so the tax is {3} for each creature attacking seat-4, and with one attacker the total is {3}. This is the figure the superseded stack 009 published wrong: it reasoned from X = 2 because the bridge that lifted that board discarded every Aura, and Abundant Growth is precisely the permanent that was missing. Sphere of Safety is a restriction of the form 'can't attack unless some condition is met', so a declaration that does not pay is an illegal declaration of attackers; because Zada requires paying a cost to attack, the active player determines the total cost to attack and it is then locked in. We can pay it: {3} is generic, generic mana takes any type, so three Mountains -- or two Mountains plus Reliquary Tower's {C} -- pays it and leaves 2 mana untapped. The corrected X therefore does not overturn (a); it raises the toll from 2 to 3 of our 5 mana, and step 7 shows the {3} buys nothing.

Adding the Aura did not disturb this arithmetic -- Abundant Growth costs {G} and contributes no white symbol -- so the X correction and the devotion reading are independent findings. steps.action: Answer (a): from the battlefield and its mana, the most damage to any ONE opponent this turn, and what prevents more.
steps.effect: THE MOST IS 3 DAMAGE, TO EXACTLY ONE OPPONENT. It is not 3 per seat and not 9 across the pod (scenario-facts drain_arithmetic: 3 opponents, 70 life across the pod, 40 / 10 / 20 per seat). By seat: seat-2 takes 3 that no BLOCK can prevent, 40 -> 37, though its eight cards and three untapped lands may still answer it in the pre-damage priority windows; seat-3 takes 3 only if it declines to block with an untapped 5/5, 10 -> 7, and if it blocks we take 0 damage and Zada goes to the command zone; seat-4 takes 3 only after we pay Sphere of Safety's {3} (X = 3) and only if it declines to block with Setessan Champion. WHAT PREVENTS MORE, precisely: (1) ONE BODY -- Zada assigns combat damage equal to her power, so 3 is the ceiling, and one creature can be declared attacking only one seat; (2) NO OUTLET -- no permanent we control has a damage-dealing ability, so the five mana cannot become a single point of damage without a card from the unknown hand; (3) Sphere of Safety taxes the 20-life seat {3} per attacking creature; (4) both low-life seats hold an untapped blocker while the only creature-less seat is the one at 40; (5) attacking taps our only creature and only blocker for the rest of the turn cycle. THE REFUTATION IS THE RESULT: this battlefield has no meaningful damage line, and that is the finding about the deck's modal board -- not a line to be manufactured.

steps.action: Begin (b). Zada's trigger condition, verbatim from the corpus: 'Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets only Zada, copy that spell for each other creature you control that the spell could target. Each copy targets a different one of those creatures.' Identify what a card in hand must satisfy for the ability to trigger at all.
steps.effect: The ability triggers only when a game event matches its trigger event, so all three conditions must hold. (i) The card must be an INSTANT or SORCERY -- no permanent card, and no activated ability, can trigger it. (ii) We must CAST it -- an object that a copy effect puts onto the stack is not cast and does not re-trigger. (iii) Every target it has must be Zada and NOTHING ELSE. Condition (iii) is the 'targets only' condition, and it is settled at cast time: the targets are declared as part of putting the spell on the stack and cannot afterwards be changed except by another spell or ability that explicitly says it can. So a spell that also targets a second creature, a player, or any other object simply never triggers the ability, and nothing after casting can repair it. Wizards' own rulings on Zada agree on (ii) and (iii) -- 'The copies that the ability creates are created on the stack, so they're not cast' and 'Zada's ability triggers whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell that targets only Zada and no other object or player' (both 2018-03-16) -- but the CR is the citation.

citations.quote: Whenever a game event or game state matches a triggered ability’s trigger event, that ability automatically triggers.
These targets are declared as part of the process of putting the spell or ability on the stack. The targets can’t be changed except by another spell or ability that explicitly says it can do so.

steps.action: Resolve the copy count FROM THIS BOARD STATE. Zada's clause copies the spell 'for each other creature you control that the spell could target'. Enumerate that set: creatures we control = {Zada, Hedron Grinder} (scenario-facts your_board.creature_bodies, one entry; other_permanents empty; the two Goblin Token entries are in the GRAVEYARD, and extras.tokens_unobserved_resolutions records 2 unobserved token resolutions for our seat which the bridge did not place on the battlefield). Creatures we control OTHER than Zada = the EMPTY SET.
steps.effect: The ability triggers, goes on the stack and resolves -- and creates ZERO COPIES, because the set it iterates over is empty. 707.10d is the governing rule for an effect of this shape ('copy ... for each player or object it could target') and supplies the target-legality filter; the empty set itself comes from Zada's own words 'each other creature you control', not from the CR. The consequence is the crux of the modal board: a perfectly chosen spell that targets only Zada is an ordinary single-target spell on a 3/3, and four mana spent on 'targets only Zada' buys exactly one instance of the effect. The engine is switched on and multiplies by one. The reconstruction this rests on was settled against the source log in the 009 review: Blasphemous Act on turn 22 destroyed every creature our seat controlled, Zada was recast on turn 23, nothing else entered under our control before the cut, and game 13 contains exactly two 'Attach to' resolutions -- both seat-4's -- so our side has no Aura the old bridge could have dropped. Any surviving body would raise the count by one per body.

steps.action: Test whether ONE card from hand could bootstrap its own copy -- an instant or sorcery that targets only Zada and also puts a body onto our battlefield as it resolves.
steps.effect: It cannot from this board, and the argument needs care. Zada's trigger is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority and becomes the topmost object, and when all players pass the top object resolves first -- so the trigger resolves, and counts our other creatures, strictly BEFORE the spell that triggered it. A body the spell itself creates on resolution therefore arrives too late to be copied for. But that ordering is NOT absolute, and 603.3 alone does not prove a general impossibility: under 603.3b, when several abilities have triggered since the last time a player received priority, each player puts the ones they control on the stack in any order they choose, so a spell with its own cast-trigger that made a body could be ordered ABOVE Zada's trigger and the body would be counted. That route is closed by ENUMERATION, not by the rule. All 30 instant and sorcery entries in this branch's 99 were read (cards.json: 30 entries, 30 copies). None has cascade and none has a token-making cast trigger. Three create creature tokens but target nothing at all (Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Empty the Warrens), so they cannot trigger Zada. Four target a creature and create a token that is NOT a creature -- three Treasure artifacts (Ancestors' Aid, Reckless Ransacking, Sudden Breakthrough) and one Role enchantment (Witch's Mark). Exactly ONE both targets a creature and creates creature tokens -- Goblin Negotiation -- and its tokens are created as THE SPELL resolves, which is after the trigger, exactly the ordering above. The four storm cards (Grapeshot, Empty the Warrens, Haze of Rage, Spreading Insurrection) copy spells, and a copy is put onto the stack rather than cast and is not a body. So no single card in the list can produce even one copy from this board. That is a fact about the 99, not a claim about what is in hand.

citations.quote: The ability becomes the topmost object on the stack.
each player, in APNAP order, puts each triggered ability they control with a trigger condition that isn’t another ability triggering on the stack in any order they choose
When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.

steps.action: Answer (b): state the MINIMUM a card in hand must do, as REQUIRED PROPERTIES rather than named cards -- the hand is unknown by construction and no card in it may be assumed.
steps.effect: From THIS board the minimum is a TWO-CARD SEQUENCE, because no single card can satisfy both halves (step 11). HALF ONE -- a card that, before the Zada spell is cast, GIVES US CONTROL of at least one creature other than Zada. Two routes qualify and the narrower phrasing would miss one: (i) a card that puts a creature onto the battlefield under our control -- a creature spell, or any token-maker, resolving first, since an object an effect puts onto the battlefield enters under that player's control; or (ii) a CONTROL-CHANGING effect, which grants control in layer 2 with nothing entering the battlefield at all. Route (ii) is live on this board: there are two untapped opposing creatures to take, seat-3's Abaddon the Despoiler (5/5) and seat-4's Setessan Champion (1/3) -- Heliod is not a creature (step 7) and is not a candidate -- and the 99 does hold a control-change sorcery, though at five mana it consumes the entire battlefield pool and leaves nothing for the second card. HALF TWO -- an instant or sorcery we CAST whose every instance of the word 'target' points at Zada and at nothing else (step 9). Two properties are load-bearing on the new body: it must be a creature we control when the TRIGGERED ABILITY resolves, and it must be a legal target for every instance of the word 'target' on that spell, since if it is not, no copy is created for it. So a spell reading 'target creature you control' works; one that restricts its target by subtype requires the body to match it; a body with shroud, or with protection that applies, is skipped and yields nothing. YIELD: each qualifying other creature adds exactly one copy, so the first body takes the multiplier from 1 to 2. MANA: from battlefield mana alone the pair must fit inside {R}{R}{R}{R}{C} -- at most four red pips, with Reliquary Tower's {C} usable only against generic (step 1, 107.4a) -- and the cheapest shape is a two-mana body-maker plus a one-mana targeting spell. A ritual in hand would lift that ceiling, but a ritual makes it a THREE-card sequence.

citations.quote: If an effect instructs a player to put an object onto the battlefield, that object enters the battlefield under that player’s control unless the effect states otherwise.
Layer 2: Control-changing effects are applied.
If the spell or ability has more than one target, each of its targets must be the same player or object.

final_state.summary: (a) THE MOST IS 3 DAMAGE, TO ONE SEAT -- and the result is a refutation. Zada, Hedron Grinder (3/3) is our only creature and no permanent we control has a damage-dealing ability, so combat is the only route and 3 power is the ceiling; the five untapped lands ({R}{R}{R}{R}{C}) have no outlet on the battlefield. Only seat-2 (40 life, three lands, no creature) cannot BLOCK it -- 40 -> 37 -- but seat-2 is also the one seat with eight cards and three untapped lands and it holds priority in both pre-damage windows (508.2, 509.2, 509.4), so the honest claim is 'damage no BLOCK can prevent', not 'guaranteed'. seat-3 (10 life) keeps Abaddon the Despoiler 5/5 untapped: a block deals it zero and destroys Zada, who then goes to the command zone (903.9a) -- a tempo loss, not the loss of the card. seat-4 (20 life) costs SPHERE OF SAFETY'S X = 3 -- three enchantments: Sphere of Safety, Heliod, Sun-Crowned, and the Aura Abundant Growth -- and Setessan Champion still blanks the attack for free. seat-4's devotion to white is 2, so Heliod is NOT a creature: it counts for X and cannot block. (b) From this board Zada's ability copies NOTHING: 'each other creature you control' is the empty set, so a perfectly chosen spell resolves as an ordinary single-target spell. No single card fixes it -- the trigger is the topmost object and resolves before the spell (603.3, and 603.3b scopes the ordering, so the impossibility is proved by enumerating all 30 instants and sorceries in the 99). The minimum is a TWO-CARD SEQUENCE: first a card that gives us control of at least one other creature -- by putting a body onto the battlefield OR by a control-change effect -- then an instant or sorcery we cast whose every 'target' is Zada, with the new body a legal target for every instance of that word. The first body takes the multiplier from 1 to 2.

What holds unchanged: zero copies from this board, the two-card minimum, and Zada not being summoning sick.

findings.note: THE MOST SERIOUS FINDING. '3 DAMAGE THAT NO BLOCK CAN PREVENT' is a second absolute, falsified by this artifact's own step 3. Step 3 establishes on 509.4 that 'a creature can even be put onto the battlefield BLOCKING after attackers are declared' and that seat-2 alone holds 8 cards (estimate) and 3 untapped lands across both pre-damage windows. A block therefore CAN prevent it. Step 4 states both halves in consecutive sentences and publishes the absolute anyway; final_state.opponents[seat-2] hardens it into the bare boolean "can_block": false and the note 'the only seat that cannot BLOCK'. The defensible scope is 'no creature on the board as lifted can block it'. Correction #2 replaced 'guaranteed' with a claim that is wrong for exactly the same reason, at all four sites.

NOT CITED, and it is the rule the headline needs. Part (a)'s answer is 3 damage to seat-2, 40 -> 37. 510.1a (cited) gives only the AMOUNT ('assigns combat damage equal to its power'); the RECIPIENT comes from 510.1b, 'An unblocked creature assigns its combat damage to the player, planeswalker, or battle it's attacking.' Nothing in the 40 slots establishes that the damage reaches the player. Eight of the 40 slots are repeats, so the room existed.

NOT CITED; a window is missing from the walk and the count is wrong. The walk names declare attackers, declare blockers, combat damage and end of combat, then asserts 'TWO of those windows sit before combat damage'. There are THREE: 507.2, 'Second, the active player gets priority', gives a full priority round in the BEGINNING OF COMBAT step, before attackers are declared — and the source log prints that step by name at part-02.log game_in_job 13. Removal cast there kills the attack before 508.1a is ever reached. The v2 step vocabulary names beginning of combat, and the under-count is in the one quantity correction #2 rests on.

NOT CITED. The load-bearing claim is that the two (three) windows are 'open to the DEFENDER'. 508.2 and 509.2 — the two rules cited — say only 'Second, the ACTIVE player gets priority.' The defender receives priority under 117.3d ('Then the next player in turn order receives priority') with 117.4 for the pass-in-succession. The step's prose says 'all players pass in turn' and cites nothing for it. 405.5 is cited in step 11 and would have half-covered this.

NOT CITED. Correction #3's second half — 'recastable at {3}{R} plus commander tax' — asserts the tax with no CR rule. 903.8: 'A commander cast from the command zone costs an additional {2} for each previous time the player casting it has cast it from the command zone that game.' scenario.seats[you].commander.casts == 1, so the recast is {3}{R} + {2} = SIX mana, a figure the artifact never states and which exceeds the entire five-mana battlefield pool. The tempo loss is understated as well as uncited.

The seat-4 line asserts 'the Champion is destroyed' with no lethal-damage citation. 704.5g is cited in step 5, for Zada only. Same rule, same step needed; step 7 carries 700.5 / 509.1a / 510.1c and stops one rule short of its own conclusion.

A CITATION DOING NO WORK, and the clearest one. Step 10 spends TWO of the 40 slots on 707.10d. The second quote ('a copy isn't created for that player or object') is the target-legality filter, which step 10's conclusion cannot use: with 'each other creature you control' an EMPTY set there is no candidate whose target legality could be tested. The filter is genuinely load-bearing in step 12, where 707.10d is cited a third time. Drop the second slot in step 10.

Verbatim and true, but duplicative: it is cited for 'combat damage equal to its power', the same proposition 510.1a carries in steps 4 and 8. 32 DISTINCT rules occupy 40 slots. The repeats: 509.1a x3 (4,5,7), 707.10d x3 (10 twice, 12), 508.1f x2 (2,8), 508.1b x2 (3,8), 510.1a x2 (4,8), 510.1c x2 (5,7), plus this 120.2a/510.1a overlap. MERGE CANDIDATES: steps 6 and 7 are both the seat-4 line and should be one step (frees 509.1a + 510.1c); step 8 is a recap that re-cites 510.1a, 508.1b and 508.1f from steps 1-4 and introduces no new rule; steps 9 and 10 are one argument (trigger condition, then copy count). Merging those three pairs takes the artifact to roughly 31 slots, inside the historical one-or-two-round band, WITH room for 510.1b, 507.2, 117.3d and 903.8.

Holds against the whole rule, but the wrong sentence is quoted. The claim is that a body 'must be a legal target for every instance of the word target, since if it is not, no copy is created for it' — that is 707.10d's fourth sentence. The quote supplied is the third ('If the spell or ability has more than one target, each of its targets must be the same player or object'), which states a different condition. Swap the quote.

Quote verbatim, applied correctly: the command-zone return is a state-based action checked at the same time as 704.5g. But the step's prose calls it 'that replacement' and 'the replacement', and the quoted text it sits beside says 'This is a state-based action.' 903.9a is an SBA under 704, not a replacement effect under 614. The wording is inherited from extras.reconstruction_notes and should not be carried into the resolution.

SPHERE OF SAFETY'S X = 3 IS CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY OF THE LIFT. I reconstructed seat-4's battlefield from the source log (part-02.log, game_in_job 13, lines 19445-21510; the cut is turn 27 precombat main). Seat-4 cast Heliod (t16), Abundant Growth on Forest 339 (t16), Sphere of Safety (t24) and Setessan Champion (t24). One further enchantment existed — ETHEREAL ARMOR, an Aura on Sythis from t12 — and it went to the graveyard at t22 when Blasphemous Act killed Sythis, Sanctum Weaver, Archon of Sun's Grace, Yenna and Ajani's Chosen. So seat-4's battlefield at the cut is exactly the eleven permanents enumerated, and the three enchantments are exactly the three named. The restriction reading and the locked-in cost are correct.

'Some objects have abilities that define the value of X' correctly settles that Sphere's X is defined, not chosen. 205.2a and 303.4 together correctly establish that a type line carrying Enchantment counts once whether or not it is also a creature or an Aura. 508.1h and 107.4b support the locked-in {3} and its payment from generic-payable red/colourless mana. One imprecision: X is determined during the declare attackers step, not in precombat main; nothing on seat-4's board can change between the two (0 cards in hand, all six lands tapped), so the figure is safe, but the step never says when X is measured.

THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL NEW CLAIM IS CORRECT, and it survived the hardest check I could put on it. 700.5 counts mana symbols of the colour among mana costs of permanents controlled. Corpus mana costs: Heliod {2}{W} = 1, Sphere of Safety {4}{W} = 1, Abundant Growth {G} = 0, Setessan Champion {2}{G} = 0, Sol Ring {1} = 0, six lands = 0. DEVOTION TO WHITE = 2 < 5, so Heliod is not a creature, counts for X, and cannot be declared as a blocker (509.1a). I specifically checked the load-bearing sub-claim that the recorded pt is PRINTED: Heliod, Sun-Crowned's printed P/T in the corpus IS 5/5, so 'the recorded 5/5 is its printed power and toughness' holds — had it been 4/4 the record would have implied a counter and the explanation would have collapsed. WotC's own Heliod ruling (2020-01-24) agrees with the conclusion: 'If a God stops being a creature, it loses the type creature and the creature type God. It continues to be a legendary enchantment.' THE RESOLVER IS RIGHT AND THE QUESTION'S PROSE IS WRONG; recording it in disagreements_with_prose rather than silently following the board is the correct handling. Two further Heliod rulings the reading is consistent with: generic and colourless symbols do not count toward devotion, and mana symbols in TEXT BOXES do not — so Abundant Growth's granted '{T}: Add one mana of any color' contributes nothing.

SETESSAN CHAMPION IS 1/3 AT THE CUT — log-verified, and this is the claim the restored Aura most threatened. Constellation would make it 2/4 if any enchantment had entered under seat-4's control after it resolved, and a 4-toughness blocker would survive Zada's 3. The log settles it: Sphere of Safety resolved first, then Setessan Champion, both in turn 24; the next enchantment to enter under seat-4's control is Sythis at turn 28 (line 1802 fires the constellation trigger), ONE TURN AFTER the cut. Abundant Growth entered at turn 16, eight turns BEFORE the Champion, so restoring the Aura does not move this. 3 damage to a 3-toughness blocker, seat-4 takes zero, Zada takes 1 and lives: correct. The step's phrase 'no enchantment entered under seat-4's control before the cut' is loose — three did — but the preceding clause scopes it to after the Champion resolved.

Summoning sickness is genuinely SETTLED, not assumed, and the log confirms the exact wording: Zada was cast and resolved in turn 23's POSTCOMBAT main (part-02.log, 'Main phase, postcombat' then 'cast Zada, Hedron Grinder' / 'Resolve Stack: Zada, Hedron Grinder - Creature 3 / 3'), with no later zone change before the turn-27 cut. 508.1a, 302.6 and 508.1f all support what they are cited for. 302.6 partly duplicates 508.1a but is the named summoning-sickness rule, which is defensible.

THE ENUMERATION CLOSES, verified card by card against the branch's cards.json: 30 instant/sorcery entries, 30 copies. No cascade. Three token-makers that target nothing (Dragon Fodder, Krenko's Command, Empty the Warrens). Four that target a creature and make a NON-creature token (Ancestors' Aid, Reckless Ransacking, Sudden Breakthrough = Treasure; Witch's Mark = Role). Exactly one that targets a creature AND makes creature tokens (Goblin Negotiation), whose tokens arrive on resolution, after the trigger. The four card shapes that could have broken it are all accounted for: the only MODAL card is Great Train Heist (spree), whose modes target either nothing or 'target opponent', so it can never satisfy 'targets only Zada'; MULTI-TARGET is handled correctly in steps 9 and 12 ('every instance of the word target'), which matches WotC's Zada ruling that a multi-target spell pointing all targets at Zada DOES trigger; a FLASH CREATURE cannot itself be the Zada spell, so it belongs to half one of step 12, not here; and no card has a token-making CAST trigger, which is the one shape 603.3b's free ordering would have let through. 603.3 and 405.5 correctly establish the trigger-before-spell ordering and 603.3b correctly scopes it — the fix asked for after 009.

The control-change route is real and correctly priced. Spreading Insurrection ({4}{R}, 'Gain control of target creature you don't control until end of turn') is the sorcery step 12 alludes to: five mana, exactly the lifted pool, so the second card is unaffordable from the battlefield — as claimed. It also cannot double as half two, since it targets a creature you do NOT control. 110.2a and 613.1b support the two routes for half one. Naming the card in the artifact would be better than 'the 99 does hold a control-change sorcery'.

ZERO COPIES CONFIRMED FROM THE LOG. Blasphemous Act at turn 22 destroyed Broadside Bombardiers, Howlsquad Heavy and Pashalik Mons on our side; Zada was recast turn 23; nothing else entered under our control before the cut. 'Each other creature you control' is the empty set. The step is honest that the empty set comes from Zada's own text and not from the CR, and honest that 707.10d supplies only the shape — that candour is correct.

THE PER-SEAT / POD DISTINCTION IS HANDLED CORRECTLY: 'not 3 per seat and not 9 across the pod', matching scenario-facts drain_arithmetic (3 opponents, 70 life, 40/10/20). The maximisation is also right: 3 is the ceiling because Zada is the only body and no permanent we control deals damage, and seat-2 is the seat with no blocker on the board as lifted, so seat-2 is where the 3 is hardest to stop. Pricing all three seats instead of overriding the authored 'attack seat-3' action, and recording the difference in disagreements_with_prose, is the right handling. SIBLING COMPARABILITY IS CLEAN: the only sibling whose figures are quoted is 009 — the superseded lift of this same board, which scenario-facts lists as same body count with the body shared. No incomparable sibling (002, 004, 005, 007, 008, 010) is quoted for a total.

OBSERVATIONS THE RESOLVER SHOULD SEE, none of which changes a published figure. (1) The lift is a faithful PRE-LAND-DROP snapshot: the log shows exactly five land plays for our seat before turn 27, so {R}{R}{R}{R}{C} is right — but in the game the pilot played a SIXTH land (Mountain 281) in that same precombat main and then cast Siege-Gang Lieutenant, Rite of Flame and Guttersnipe postcombat. The artifact's 'a floor on the turn's mana, not a ceiling' caveat names the six rituals; it does not name GREAT TRAIN HEIST ({R}, spree +{2}{R} for an additional combat phase), which is the card in the 99 that actually breaks the 3-damage ceiling, nor Guttersnipe, the card that was in fact in hand. (2) THE LIFTED GRAVEYARDS ARE INCOMPLETE and the open question does not say so: ours omits Howlsquad Heavy and Pashalik Mons, seat-4's omits Ethereal Armor, Sanctum Weaver, Archon of Sun's Grace, Yenna and Ajani's Chosen, and seat-3's Abaddon the Despoiler is recorded on the battlefield AND in the graveyard. Nothing in the resolution rests on a graveyard, and assumptions[0] does warn the lift may be incomplete elsewhere, but this is a second live bridge gap beside the Aura one and belongs in the same open question. (3) NO STEP CONTRADICTS A WotC RULING: Heliod's 2020-01-24 rulings, Setessan Champion's constellation ruling and all eight Zada rulings agree with the artifact; the rulings section is PRESENT, not absent.
